relationships.subject: AGEs
relationships.evidence_quote: The engagement of RAGE by AGEs initiates a cascade of intracellular signaling events that perpetuate cellular dysfunction.

relationships.subject: RAGE
relationships.evidence_quote: Key pathways activated downstream of RAGE include nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) and various mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs)

relationships.subject: NF-κB pathway
relationships.evidence_quote: Activation of NF-κB upregulates numerous pro-inflammatory genes, resulting in the production of cytokines (e.g., TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) that fuel inflammation

relationships.subject: AGEs
relationships.evidence_quote: AGE accumulation promotes RAGE expression, which in turn sensitizes cells to further AGE-mediated damage

relationships.subject: AGEs
relationships.evidence_quote: Emerging evidence indicates that AGE-RAGE interaction can directly activate and sensitize these neurons, potentially contributing to the hyperalgesia

key_findings: Review: the AGE-RAGE axis drives NF-κB/MAPK inflammation, MMP-mediated ECM degradation and a feed-forward AGE-RAGE loop in periodontitis.
Proposes AGE-RAGE activation of RAGE-expressing sensory neurons (neuropeptides SP and CGRP) as a neuro-immune route to periodontal pain.
